fixes.explanation: Close, baker, but this one flips it around. The voice in the psalm says, "When I choose a time, I will judge fairly." So the one speaking is the one who chooses the time. The people don't get to set it, and I'd bet nobody in my bakery gets to set my oven timer either, because I'm the one who set it wrong last time.

Yes, baker. In the psalm, the voice says, "When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars." Everything is shaking, and the voice is the one holding the pillars up. I once rattled one cookie sheet and panicked for an hour, so I respect this.

You got it, baker. After saying where it doesn't come from, the song says, "…but it is God who judges…" So the source isn't a direction on the map. It's God. No east, no west, no desert, just God. I've been checking every corner of my bakery for the answer to things for years, and it turns out the answer was never in the corner.

Not quite, baker. The verse says the wicked "…drink it down to the dregs." The dregs are the very last bits at the bottom of the cup. That's not a sip, and it isn't set back down. They drink it all the way to the bottom.

That's how it ends, baker. In the last verse, the voice says, "All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted." The wicked horns get cut off, and the righteous horns get lifted up. It's a clear last line.
